title: Pod backoff surge + ephemeral disk corruption — oncall notes
content:
Quick summary:
- During 2025-11-03 02:13 UTC we observed a cluster-wide spike of Pod CrashLoopBackOff / ImagePullBackOff-like symptoms concentrated in a single AZ. Pods failed to start with repeated CrashLoopBackOff spikes for stateful and stateless workloads that use local-emptyDir and hostPath volumes.
- Root observable: multiple nodes in AZ eu-west-1b reported kernel I/O errors and remounted root/ephemeral partitions as read-only -> kubelet began failing to write container logs and the container runtime (containerd) hit repeated errors causing pod restart loops.
- Impact: ~18 nodes affected, ~240 pods flapping for 40 minutes. No control-plane etcd corruption observed.

On-call timeline (compressed):
- 02:10 UTC: Pager fired (CRITICAL): increased CrashLoopBackOff rate metric and pod restart rate alert.
- 02:13 UTC: On-call (Aisha) triaged, looked at alerts, pulled up 1m restart-rate chart and nodes affected list (filter: kube_node:condition_readonly_filesystem==true).
- 02:16 UTC: SSH into one affected node (ip: 10.12.7.42). journalctl -u kubelet showed repeated errors: "Write failed: Read-only file system" and containerd logs showed: "failed to write container log: write /var/log/containers/…: read-only file system". dmesg showed repeated I/O errors on nvme0n1.
- 02:20 UTC: Cordon + drain attempted for the node, drain hung due to local pods and missing --delete-local-data flag. We used: kubectl drain ip-10-12-7-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- 02:24 UTC: Noticed other nodes showing similar kernel I/O traces. Increased severity and paged storage engineers.
- 02:28 UTC: Remediation action: emergency autoscaling of replacement nodes in the same ASG and manual detach of likely-corrupt EBS volumes (where applicable). For NVMe-backed ephemeral, we initiated node reboot after cordon/drain.
- 02:35 UTC: Node rebooted, kernel brought device back read-write temporarily but errors resumed on some nodes.
- 02:50 UTC: After replacing 10 nodes (cordon -> drain -> terminate -> let ASG replace), cluster stabilized; pod restart rate returned to baseline by 03:00 UTC.

Key logs & commands (notes-to-self / for runbook):
- kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -o wide | grep CrashLoopBackOff
- kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, conditions: .status.conditions}' | grep ReadOnly
- journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | sed -n '/Read-only file system/,$p'
- sudo dmesg | egrep -i 'I/O error|nvme|ext4\|xfs'
- sudo lsblk -f && sudo mount | grep /var/lib/containerd
- containerd logs: sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200 | tail -n 80
- quick check: sudo touch /tmp/test && echo ok >/tmp/test (fails when FS ro)

Observed patterns and evidence:
- dmesg on affected nodes: repeated "nvme0n1: I/O error, dev write sector" followed by ext4 remount as "(ro,"
- Kubelet errors: failed to write container log; kubelet reported image gc and eviction messages around same timeframe
- No عمومی (widespread) network failures; control plane healthy, etcd quorum stable; API latency modestly increased due to flapping pod churn.
- Affected nodes were all in the same AZ and on a single instance type (c6i-metal-ephemeral) which uses local NVMe for ephemeral storage.

Immediate mitigations that worked (short-term):
- Cordon + drain (with --delete-local-data) -> terminate instance in ASG -> let autoscaling provision a fresh node. This removed the read-only device from the pool quickly.
- For nodes where reboot briefly cleared error, eviction of pods and kubelet restart sometimes returned the node to RW, but reoccurred: underlying device showed recurring I/O errors.
- Temporary cluster-level autoscaling policy increased replacement capacity for AZ eu-west-1b for 20 minutes to avoid scheduling pressure during replacement.

Hypothesis (root cause):
- Most likely: NVMe device firmware bug / ephemeral block device hardware degradation triggered by a kernel NVMe error path that remounted the fs read-only. The pattern (same instance type, same AZ) points to either faulty hardware batch or a host-level firmware update rolled out by the cloud provider in that AZ.
- Alternative: a noisy workload causing pathological I/O pattern (but affected nodes had mixed workloads; not all were heavy I/O consumers).

Why this was tricky / what caused delayed resolution:
- Symptoms started at application layer (CrashLoopBackOff) rather than node-level alert, so initial correlation took time.
- Draining nodes with local data requires --delete-local-data, operator hesitation slowed initial drain.
- Some nodes returned to RW on reboot (masking recurrent nature) causing a stop-gap cadence of reboots instead of full replacement.

Runbook draft updates (actionable edits):
1) Add a new play for "Read-only filesystem on node (ephemeral storage)":
   - Signal: kubelet logs show "Read-only file system" or dmesg shows I/O errors; pods flapping with CrashLoopBackOff and only on specific AZ/instance type.
   - Immediate steps:
     a) Cordon node: kubectl cordon <node>
     b) Drain with deletion of local data: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
     c) If node uses ephemeral NVMe (instance metadata tag / label), terminate instance in ASG / MIG -> do not attempt in-place repair.
     d) If using attached volumes, snapshot + detach and investigate.
     e) If multiple nodes affected in same AZ/instance type, coordinate with cloud provider support and escalate (open cloud ticket, include dmesg output and instance IDs).
   - Do not: attempt live filesystem repair on nodes still in service; prefer remove-and-replace.

2) Add automatic alert rule: if >5% of nodes in AZ show "Read-only file system" within 10m, escalate to sev2 and page storage on-call.
3) Add a healthcheck monitor on nodes detecting kernel I/O errors via node-exporter dmesg scrape or journald exporter; include in runbook linking to remediation steps.
4) Document how to safely drain stateful workloads that use local-emptyDir with minimal data loss (backups, brief window).

Post-incident follow-ups / TODOs (owner assignments):
- [Aisha] Collect sample dmesg + journal logs from 6 representative nodes, upload to incident artifact bucket and link to JIRA-INC-4521. (done, pending analysis)
- [Marcus] Open cloud support ticket with provider, include instance IDs, dmesg, times — ask if there was firmware push or noisy host hardware. (in progress)
- [Li Wei] Run a targeted cluster check next week to detect nodes with high SMART/NVMe error counts; propose nightly probe for first-failure-time aggregation. (todo)
- [Platform] Add labeling automation: add instance-type and ephemeral-storage=true labels so we can quickly filter future incidents. (proposal)

Notes / unanswered questions:
- Was there a rolling maintenance event in eu-west-1b at the time? Ask cloud provider.
- Should we change eviction thresholds for ephemeral-storage to be more aggressive for affected instance types? Risk: premature eviction for normal bursts. Consider adaptive thresholds based on instance type.

Slack snippets (for timeline reconstruction):
- @oncall: seeing CrashLoopBackOff spike in eu-west-1b, most pods failing with "Read-only file system" in kubelet logs
- @storage: NVMe I/O errors on a set of c6i-metal-ephemeral -> coordinating with cloud

Rough runbook checklist (copyable):
1) Identify affected nodes: kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep -E 'NotReady|ReadOnly'
2) SSH into one node, capture: sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg.out; sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 > /tmp/kubelet.log
3) Cordon: kubectl cordon <node>
4) Drain: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
5) Terminate instance in ASG and tag instance-id with incident id (JIRA-INC-4521)
6) For attached volumes: snapshot before detach (aws ec2 create-snapshot) and create ticket for long-term storage investigation

Follow-up postmortem items for next retro:
- Determine if firmware/hardware rollout correlated; obtain cloud provider statement.
- Add automated detection rule for kernel I/O errors aggregated by AZ + instance-type.
- Add a short playbook for automated replacement of read-only nodes (ASG runbook).

End of notes. This doc is intentionally informal; move to a postmortem template if we escalate to sev1 retrospective.
